deals.headline: Farhad Moshiri buys 49.9% of Everton
deals.summary: Everton confirmed former Arsenal shareholder Farhad Moshiri would acquire 49.9% of the club, subject to Premier League approval; the price was only reported (about £200m), not stated.

deals.evidence: Everton Football Club has been acquired by Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited (Roundhouse), an entity within The Friedkin Group (TFG).
deals.headline: The Friedkin Group completes Everton takeover
deals.investor: Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited (The Friedkin Group)
deals.summary: Roundhouse Capital Holdings, within The Friedkin Group, bought Farhad Moshiri's majority stake held through Blue Heaven Holdings after Premier League approval of a 98.8% acquisition. BBC reported the deal as believed to be worth in excess of £400m; no price was stated by the parties.

deals.evidence: has agreed a £350m package with a consortium of blue-chip institutional lenders, rearranging the build project’s borrowing
deals.headline: Everton agree £350m long-term stadium refinancing
deals.investor: Consortium of institutional lenders (arranged with JP Morgan)
deals.summary: The Friedkin Group arranged a £350m package with a consortium of institutional lenders to replace the previous ownership's borrowing for the Bramley-Moore Dock (Hill Dickinson) stadium; the club's 2024/25 accounts describe it as repayable over 30 years with JP Morgan Chase.

deals.evidence: the conversion of £450.7m of shareholder loans into equity
deals.headline: £450.7m of shareholder loans converted to equity
deals.investor: Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited (The Friedkin Group)
deals.summary: As part of the financial reset following the change of ownership, Everton repaid existing borrowings, converted £450.7m of shareholder loans into equity and introduced a new revolving credit facility.

name: Everton Football Club
notes: Companies House PSC: Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited (15992615), ownership of shares 75% or more, notified 18 December 2024. Stake: Premier League states 98.8%; BBC reports Roundhouse would rise to 99.5% through further debt-to-equity conversions (not recorded as a stake). The Friedkin Group is a family-controlled private conglomerate (Dan Friedkin), so ownership_type is individual_family, not institutional. Takeover price only reported ('believed to be worth in excess of £400m', BBC), so amount left null. Revenue breakdown: club gives matchday (gate receipts £20.3m) and broadcast (£129.2m); commercial is split into sponsorship/advertising/merchandising £24.3m and other commercial £22.9m, which are not summed. Wages: club gives only the wage-to-turnover ratio (74%). Capacity was 52,888 at design; post-construction figure 52,769 (Yahoo/Liverpool Echo). evertonfc.com is a client-rendered app that cannot be read by fetch, so club statements are cited from premierleague.com reproductions. Forbes (May 2026) also gives revenue $255M (£197M) and operating income -$15M for 2024-25 and debt/value 49%. Not found: shirt sponsor, kit supplier, chair title as currently held, attendance, social counts with dates, stadium ownership.

owners.evidence: The Premier League Board has approved The Friedkin Group’s 98.8 per cent acquisition of Everton Football Club

ownership_summary: Owned since 19 December 2024 by Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited, an entity within Dan Friedkin's The Friedkin Group (also owner of AS Roma), which bought Farhad Moshiri's majority stake held through Blue Heaven Holdings; the Premier League approved a 98.8% acquisition. Roundhouse is the registered person with significant control (75% or more).
